blogs.title: Breathe Under the Bedrock: Central Hypoventilation Syndromes Tying Back‑to‑Neurosurgery
blogs.description: Explore how cerebellar tonsillar descent impairs automatic respiratory control—giving rise to an acquired form of Ondine’s curse—in patients who otherwise breathe normally during wakefulness. We’ll walk through clinical clues (evidence‑free choking at night without dyspnea), share physiological rationale behind absent interoception during severe desaturations, outline key polysomnographic differentiators from obstructive apneas, and discuss how this informs timely referral for posterior fossa decompression.

blogs.title: Choking Without a Shadow: Neurogenic Dysphagia as a Fingerprint for Posterior Fossa Compression
blogs.description: Recount why repeated non‑mechanical choking episodes should trigger neuro‑odyssey rather than repeated ENT workups. Highlight swallow physiology—solid/liquid equivalence signals neurogenic dysphagia—and guide practitioners through video‑fluoroscopic swallow studies’ pearls that hint at underlying brainstem pathology like Chiari malformation. Emphasize early multidisciplinary counseling (swallow therapy, nutrition trials) before neurosurgical escalation.

blogs.title: A Seatbelt That Struck Deep: Post‑Traumatic Secondary versus Congenital Chiari Malformations
blogs.description: Dissect the continuum between primary developmental risk versus head‐injury–induced tonsillar herniation seen in adults long after trauma. Review radiologic clues that debate true secondary etiology—including crowded foramen magnum seen on old CTs—and consider how age at injury, symptom latency (e.g., decades before choking emerges), and associated signs help us decide whether accelerated CSF obstruction warrants surgical intervention.

blogs.title: Silent Nights – Unmasking True Sleep Apnea Severity With Full Polysomnography
blogs.description: Detail why Type III sleep studies can grossly underestimate auto­regulatory failure when they lack EEG gating—and how surgeons should interpret “low” AHI numbers against a backdrop of adult sudden oxygen falls recognised by patients’ home monitors or emergency encounters. Illustrate stepwise escalation from simple pulse oximetry trends up through full Type I polysomnography inclusive of capnography, highlighting thresholds that should prompt surgical consideration.

blogs.title: Hold It or Take It Out? Balancing Conservative Monitoring Versus Posterior Fossa Decompression In Symptomatic CMI
blogs.description: Chart evidence‐based criteria steering clinicians toward watchful waiting versus operative rescue in patients presenting with choking episodes or intermittent central hypoxemia linked to cerebellar tonsillar descent over 10 mm below the foramen magnum. Compare surgical outcomes—including symptom regression versus complication rates—against progressive clinical deterioration patterns such as recurrent severe desaturation while awake or at rest.
